lem-boundary-homology-cokernels-surject-:
## Statement

Let $R$ be a commutative unital ring. Let $W$ and $X$ be compact manifolds with supplied boundary collars and decompositions $\partial W=A\sqcup D$ and $\partial X=A\sqcup B$, where each summand is a union of boundary components. Glue the two copies of $A$ by a supplied homeomorphism, obtaining $Y=W\cup_A X$ with $\partial Y=D\sqcup B$. All homology below has constant coefficients $R$. Suppose
$$H_1(A;R)\longrightarrow H_1(X;R)\ \text{is injective},\qquad H_2(B;R)\longrightarrow H_2(X;R)\ \text{is surjective}.$$
Then inclusion of $W$ induces a well-defined surjection
$$\frac{H_2(W;R)}{\operatorname{im}H_2(\partial W;R)} \twoheadrightarrow \frac{H_2(Y;R)}{\operatorname{im}H_2(\partial Y;R)}.$$
In particular, if $R$ is a field and the first quotient is finite dimensional, the dimension of the second quotient is at most that of the first. No injectivity assumption on $H_2(A;R)\to H_2(X;R)$, orientability, or choice principle is needed.
lem-explicit-integral-seifert-matrices-r:
## Statement

For every $0<\theta_0<\pi$ and every open interval $I\subset(0,\pi)$ containing $\theta_0$, there is an explicit integral $8\times8$ matrix $V$ with $\det(V-V^T)=1$ such that the finite Hermitian matrix
$$H_\theta(V)=(1-e^{i\theta})V+(1-e^{-i\theta})V^T$$
has signature $2$ at $\theta_0$ and signature zero for all $\theta\in[0,\pi]\setminus I$. Its signature takes only the values $0,1,2$ on $[0,\pi]$ and is invariant under $\theta\mapsto-\theta$. Moreover, its signature equals $2$ throughout an open interval containing $\theta_0$. No choice principle, classification of Seifert forms, realization by a knot, or infinite-dimensional spectral theorem is assumed.
lem-finite-disk-band-knot-longitudes-lie:
## Statement

Supply a finite polygonal disk-band oriented Seifert surface, its local ambient smooth roundings, and the resulting smooth oriented knot $K=\partial F\subset S^3$. Supply a compatible closed product tube $N(K)$, a positive meridian $\mu$, a preferred zero longitude $\lambda$ obtained by trimming and paralleling $F$, and peripheral base paths. Put $X_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and let $M(K)$ be its zero-longitude filling. Then
$$H_1(X_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu],\qquad \lambda\in\pi_1(X_K)^{(2)}.$$
Both $\pi_1(X_K)$ and $\pi_1(M(K))$ are normally generated by their marked meridian images. These conclusions use no choice principle. The finite model and tubes are part of the input; no existence theorem for a neighborhood of an arbitrary locally flat surface is assumed.
lem-finite-free-chain-evaluation-over-or:
## Statement

Let $R$ be an associative unital ring with $1\ne0$ and no zero divisors, embedded as a unital subring in a division ring $K$, let $N=K/R$ as a right $R$-module, and let $C_*$ be a chain complex of right $R$-modules with $C_0,C_1$ finite free and $C_j=0$ for $j<0$. If either $H_0(C_*)=0$ or every right ideal of $R$ is principal, then restriction to cycles induces an isomorphism of abelian groups
$$\kappa:H^1(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,N))\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_1(C_*),N).$$
If the coefficient Hom groups carry a compatible commuting left action, this is an isomorphism for that action as well. No choice principle is assumed.
lem-finite-standard-skew-seifert-matrice:
## Statement

Let $g\ge0$ and let $W$ be an integral $2g\times2g$ matrix satisfying
$$W-W^T=\bigoplus_{j=1}^g\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
A finite construction produces a compact connected smooth oriented surface $F\subset S^3$ with one boundary component and an ordered basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ such that
$$\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)=W_{ij}.$$
Here $a_i^+$ is a sufficiently small push in the positive oriented normal direction to $F$. The construction uses a finite disk-and-band diagram, finitely many full twists and pairwise clasps, and finite local smoothing. It needs no choice axiom, abstract classification of Seifert forms, generic-projection theorem for arbitrary curves, or normal-neighborhood theorem for locally flat surfaces in four dimensions.
lem-killing-deep-derived-normal-subgroup:
## Statement

Let $r\ge0$, let $G$ be a group, and let $N\triangleleft G$ satisfy $N\subseteq G^{(r)}$, where $G^{(0)}=G$ and $G^{(i+1)}=[G^{(i)},G^{(i)}]$. Put $H=G/N$ and let $q:G\to H$ be the quotient. Supply a finite list of commutative unital rings $R_0,\ldots,R_{r-1}$. For a group $L$ define, through index $r$,
$$P^0L=L,\qquad P^{i+1}L=\ker\!\left(P^iL\longrightarrow (P^iL/[P^iL,P^iL])\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R_i\right).$$
The tensor map sends an abelianized class $a$ to $a\otimes1$. Then for $0\le i\le r$, $N\subseteq P^iG$ and the restriction of $q$ induces
$$P^iG/N\cong P^iH,\qquad G/P^iG\cong H/P^iH.$$
For $0\le i<r$ it also induces
$$P^iG/P^{i+1}G\cong P^iH/P^{i+1}H.$$
These are the actual natural quotient maps. Every $P^iL$ is characteristic in $L$ and contains $L^{(i)}$. The same $q$ induces $G/G^{(r)}\cong H/H^{(r)}$. If all $R_i=\mathbb Q$, then $G/P^rG$ is PTFA. A final choice $R_i=\mathbb F_p$ is allowed in the quotient conclusions, but no PTFA assertion is made for such a series. No choice axiom is assumed.
lem-normal-cover-local-homology-detects-:
## Statement

Let $W$ be a connected Hausdorff space with a supplied basis of contractible open neighborhoods, $o\in W$, $\pi=\pi_1(W,o)$, and $N\triangleleft\pi$. Put $G=\pi/N$ and let $k$ be any commutative unital ring. Use first-loop-first concatenation in $\pi$. There is a canonical based normal path-class cover $p:W_N\to W$ with $\pi_1(W_N)=N$, whose right deck action is
$$[\gamma]\cdot g=[a^{-1}*\gamma]\quad\text{when }a\in\pi\text{ represents }g.$$
Let $\mathcal R_x$ be the free $k$-module on $p^{-1}(x)$, with its induced right $k[G]$ action and transport along lifted paths. Each fiber is free of rank one as a right $k[G]$-module. Its base fiber is identified with $k[G]$ by the constant-path lift. Thus transport around a based loop $a$ is left multiplication by its quotient image $g^{-1}$.

For this specified right local system, the actual singular chain complex is naturally isomorphic to $C_*(W_N;k)$ as a complex of right $k[G]$-modules, and there is a natural isomorphism
$$H_1(W;\mathcal R)\cong (N/[N,N])\otimes_{\mathbb Z}k.$$
The right action on the last group is $[u]\otimes c\mapsto[a^{-1}ua]\otimes c$ for $g=[a]\in G$. A based loop $u\in N$ with coefficient $1$ corresponds to $[u]\otimes1$. In particular it represents zero in $H_1(W;\mathcal R)$ exactly when it lies in the kernel of $N\to(N/[N,N])\otimes_{\mathbb Z}k$. Taking $N=P^s\pi$ gives exactly the next mixed-series kernel $P^{s+1}\pi$ with coefficient ring $k$. For a based continuous map carrying $N$ into a normal subgroup $N\prime$ of the target fundamental group, these identifications commute with its induced homology maps and quotient-group coefficient maps. This includes every connected Hausdorff manifold, with boundary allowed, and every connected finite polyhedron. No finite CW structure, compactness, finite generation of $\pi$, or choice principle is assumed.
lem-ore-localization-is-flat-and-detects:
## Statement

Let $R$ be a unital ring with $1\ne0$ and no zero divisors. Suppose both Ore conditions hold: any two nonzero elements have a nonzero common right multiple and a nonzero common left multiple. Let $R\subseteq K$ be a unital embedding into a division ring such that every element of $K$ is a right fraction $as^{-1}$ with $a\in R$ and $0\ne s\in R$.

For every right $R$-module $M$, the right $K$-module $M\otimes_RK$ is represented by fractions $[m,s]$ with $m\in M$ and $0\ne s\in R$, corresponding to $m\otimes s^{-1}$. The equality criterion is
$$[m,s]=[n,t]\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{there exist }0\ne u,v\in R\text{ with }su=tv\text{ and }mu=nv.$$
In particular, $[m,s]=0$ if and only if $ma=0$ for some $0\ne a\in R$. Thus the kernel of $M\to M\otimes_RK$, $m\mapsto m\otimes1$, is exactly the set of elements with a nonzero right annihilator, and $M\otimes_RK=0$ if and only if every element of $M$ has a nonzero right annihilator.

The functor $-\otimes_RK$ is exact on arbitrary right $R$-modules, so $K$ is flat as a left $R$-module. For every chain complex $C_\bullet$ of right $R$-modules, the canonical map gives a natural isomorphism
$$H_i(C_\bullet)\otimes_RK\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H_i(C_\bullet\otimes_RK)$$
for every integer $i$. No finite-generation, finite-presentation or boundedness assumption on the modules or complexes is required.

The corresponding left-module assertions also hold: $K$ is flat as a right $R$-module, $1\otimes m$ is zero in $K\otimes_RM$ precisely when $am=0$ for some $0\ne a\in R$, and $K\otimes_R-$ commutes with the homology of arbitrary left-module chain complexes. All assertions require no choice axiom.
lem-primitive-laurent-annihilators-prese:
## Statement

Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$ and $\Lambda_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q[t,t^{-1}]$. Let $\Delta\in\Lambda$ be nonzero and primitive, meaning that the greatest common divisor of its finitely many integer coefficients is one. Define
$$T_\Delta=\{x\in\mathbb Q(t)/\Lambda:\Delta x=0\}.$$
The natural map $\mathbb Q(t)/\Lambda\to\mathbb Q(t)/\Lambda_{\mathbb Q}$ is injective on $T_\Delta$.

For a prime $p$ such that $\bar\Delta\ne0$ in $\Lambda_p=\mathbb F_p[t,t^{-1}]$, there is a well-defined additive reduction map
$$\rho_{p,\Delta}:T_\Delta\longrightarrow\mathbb F_p(t)/\Lambda_p,\qquad [a/\Delta]\longmapsto[\bar a/\bar\Delta],\quad a\in\Lambda.$$
It satisfies $\rho_{p,\Delta}(b x)=\bar b\,\rho_{p,\Delta}(x)$ for $b\in\Lambda$. For every nonzero $x\in T_\Delta$, one can compute a nonzero integer $D$ from $\Delta$ and a chosen representative $a/\Delta$ such that $\rho_{p,\Delta}(x)\ne0$ for every prime $p\nmid D$. No choice principle or factorization theorem for arbitrary rings is assumed. This is a map on the specified annihilated quotient module; no global reduction homomorphism from $\mathbb Q(t)$ to $\mathbb F_p(t)$ is asserted.
lem-principal-boundary-chain-evaluation-:
## Statement

Let $R$ be an associative unital ring with $1\ne0$ and no zero divisors, embedded as a unital subring in a division ring $K$, put $N=K/R$ as a right $R$-module, and let $C_*$ be a right $R$-module chain complex concentrated in nonnegative degrees. Supply an identification $C_0=R$. If the right ideal $\operatorname{im}(d_1)$ is principal, restriction to cycles gives an isomorphism
$$H^1(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,N))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_1(C_*),N).$$
Neither a principal ideal domain hypothesis on $R$ nor a choice principle is required.
lem-subgroup-group-ring-extension-is-fai:
## Statement

Let $k$ be a commutative unital ring and $H\le G$ a subgroup. Set $A=k[H]\subseteq B=k[G]$. Extension $-\otimes_A B$ on right modules is exact and faithful, and for each right $A$-module $M$ the map $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ is split injective as an $A$-module map. For every right-$A$ chain complex $C_*$, without a boundedness or finiteness assumption, there is the natural isomorphism
$$H_i(C_*)\otimes_A B\cong H_i(C_*\otimes_A B).$$
The corresponding left-module assertions hold with the tensor factors reversed.

Suppose additionally that $A$ and $B$ have $1\ne0$, no zero divisors and both Ore conditions, and are embedded in their right-fraction division rings $F$ and $K$, respectively. Then the inclusion $A\to B$ extends uniquely to an injective ring map $F\to K$. Under this identification,
$$F\cap B=A,\qquad F/A\longrightarrow K/B\text{ is injective as an }A\text{-bimodule map}.$$
All assertions require no choice principle, including when $G/H$ is infinite. No splitting of a group extension is assumed.
lem-cdr-smooth-s4-complement-is-standard:
## Statement

Let B be a smooth 4-ball embedded in the standard smooth 4-sphere S⁴. The closure of S⁴\B is diffeomorphic to the standard 4-ball. This is the special smooth Schoenflies complement assertion used after a capped contractible 4-manifold has been identified with standard S⁴; it does not assert the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture.
lem-choice-free-low-degree-coefficient-b:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a compact connected Hausdorff manifold with a basepoint, and let $0\to\mathcal A\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{q}\mathcal C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of local systems of abelian groups on $M$. There is a natural coefficient Bockstein making the sequence
$$H^1(M;\mathcal B)\xrightarrow{q_*}H^1(M;\mathcal C)\xrightarrow{\beta}H^2(M;\mathcal A)\xrightarrow{i_*}H^2(M;\mathcal B)$$
exact at its two middle terms. In particular $\beta$ is an isomorphism if $H^1(M;\mathcal B)=H^2(M;\mathcal B)=0$. No choice principle is assumed. If the local systems and maps have a commuting coefficient-ring action, the sequence and Bockstein respect it.
lem-explicit-disk-band-knots-realize-arb:
## Statement

For every $0<\theta_0<\pi$ and open interval $I\subset(0,\pi)$ containing $\theta_0$, there is a smooth oriented knot $K$ with a supplied compact connected oriented genus-four Seifert surface, ordered integral homology basis and positive-push Seifert matrix $V$ such that
$$\operatorname{sign}\bigl((1-e^{i\theta_0})V+(1-e^{-i\theta_0})V^T\bigr)=2,$$
and the same signature is zero for all $\theta\in[0,\pi]\setminus I$. It is nonnegative on $[0,\pi]$, constant equal to two on a neighborhood of $\theta_0$, and symmetric under $\theta\mapsto-\theta$. The surface, basis and knot are given by finite disk-band data; no choice principle or algebraic concordance classification is assumed.
lem-finite-prime-families-have-explicit-:
## Statement

Supply distinct odd primes $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ with $m\ge1$ and positive real numbers $C_1,\ldots,C_m$. Put $\omega_j=\exp(2\pi i/p_j)$. A finite construction gives smooth oriented knots $K_1,\ldots,K_m$, each with a supplied connected one-boundary oriented Seifert surface and ordered integral basis with exact positive-push matrix $V_i$. Define its chosen-surface signature function by
$$s_i(z)=\operatorname{sign}\bigl((1-z)V_i+(1-\bar z)V_i^T\bigr),\qquad z\in S^1.$$
There are positive integers $N_i$ such that
$$s_i(\omega_i)=s_i(\omega_i^{-1})=2N_i>C_i,$$
while $s_i(\omega_i^r)=0$ when $r\not\equiv\pm1\pmod{p_i}$, and $s_i(\omega_j^r)=0$ for all integers $r$ when $j\ne i$. Each $s_i$ is nonnegative on the entire unit circle. In particular,
$$\frac1{p_i}\sum_{r=0}^{p_i-1}s_i(\omega_i^r)=\frac{4N_i}{p_i}>\frac{2C_i}{p_i},\qquad \frac1{p_j}\sum_{r=0}^{p_j-1}s_i(\omega_j^r)=0\quad(j\ne i).$$
The surface for $K_i$ has genus $4N_i$. No choice principle, concordance classification, cabling formula, signature-to-rho formula or uniform analytic bound is assumed.
thm-compact-manifolds-have-finite-presen:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a compact connected Hausdorff manifold, with boundary allowed, and $o\in M$. Supply any finite list of based loops $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_\ell$. There is a finite connected two-dimensional CW complex $K$ with one vertex $v$, a based map $f:(K,v)\to(M,o)$ inducing an isomorphism on fundamental groups, and marked oriented one-cells which $f$ parametrizes by the specified loops. In particular $\pi_1(M,o)$ is finitely presented without a choice axiom.

For any normal subgroup $N\triangleleft\pi_1(M,o)$ and commutative unital ring $k$, use on $M$ the associated right $k[\pi_1(M)/N]$ normal-cover system and on $K$ its pullback. The actual induced map on $H_1$ with these coefficients is an isomorphism. No finite CW type, triangulation or smoothing of $M$ is asserted.
thm-compact-betti-one-manifolds-have-pri:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a compact connected Hausdorff manifold, with boundary allowed, with a specified based loop $\mu$ whose integral homology class freely generates $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$. Let $\phi:\pi_1(M)\to\mathbb Z$ be the abelianization taking $\mu$ to $1$, put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$, and use its associated normal-cover right coefficient system, whose transport around a loop $a$ is left multiplication by $t^{-\phi(a)}$ in the based fiber.

There is a finite Laurent matrix $A(t)$ such that
$$H_1(M;\Lambda)\cong\operatorname{coker}A(t),$$
naturally on changing the constant coefficient ring from $\mathbb Z$ to any commutative unital ring $k$. More precisely the actual coefficient map gives
$$H_1(M;\Lambda)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}k\cong H_1(M;k[t,t^{-1}]).$$
There is a polynomial $\Delta(t)\in\mathbb Z[t]$ with $\Delta(0)\ne0$ and $\Delta(1)=1$ annihilating $H_1(M;\Lambda)$; its coefficient image annihilates $H_1(M;k[t,t^{-1}])$ for every $k$. In particular $\Delta$ is primitive and its reduction modulo any prime is nonzero. No choice principle, finite CW type, triangulation, smoothness or Seifert presentation for $M$ is assumed.
thm-ptfa-augmentation-detects-projective:
## Statement

Let $k$ be a commutative field and $G$ a PTFA group. For every homomorphism $f:P\to Q$ between projective right-$k[G]$ modules, if
$$f\otimes1:P\otimes_{k[G]}k\longrightarrow Q\otimes_{k[G]}k$$
is injective under the augmentation $k[G]\to k$, then $f$ is injective. Projective means the lifting property for surjections, applied to right modules; it does not mean a supplied free basis. Thus this is the right-module defining property of Strebel's class $D(k)$. The left-module version holds too.

Moreover, if $k[G]\subseteq K$ is a supplied division ring of Ore fractions, every finite matrix $T$ over $k[G]$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{rank}_K(T\otimes K)\ge\operatorname{rank}_k(\varepsilon T).$$
Both assertions require no choice axiom. The group need not be finitely generated, its series need not be normal in all of $G$, and its successive extensions need not split.
def-cdr-satellite-concordance-categories:
## Definition

Let knots be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented S³ and let I=[0,1]. Let C_sm be their smooth concordance classes, where equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in S³×I. Let C_top be their locally flat topological concordance classes in that product. Let C_ex be their exotic-smooth concordance classes: equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W together with an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of pairs (W,∂W)≅(S³×I,S³×{0,1}) matching the endpoint knots. For a nonzero integer n set R_n=Z[1/|n|]. Let C^{1/n} be the classes under equivalence witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W with boundary the two standard endpoint 3-spheres such that each boundary inclusion induces an isomorphism H_i(S³;R_n)→H_i(W;R_n) for every i. A knot is pseudo-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold homeomorphic to B⁴, with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³. A knot is Z[1/|n|]-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold B with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³ and with H_i(B;R_n)≅H_i(B⁴;R_n) for every i; such a B is an R_n-homology 4-ball. These are sets of equivalence classes; this definition alone asserts no group structure.
lem-ptfa-finite-projective-basechange-pr:
## Statement

Let $k$ be a commutative field, let $G$ be PTFA, put $A=k[G]$, and supply its Ore fraction division ring $K$. Subscripts $k$ and $K$ mean tensor base change along augmentation $A\to k$ and inclusion $A\to K$, respectively.

For every finitely generated projective right-$A$ module $P$,
$$\dim_K P_K=\dim_k P_k<\infty.$$
For a homomorphism $f:P\to Q$ between such modules,
$$\dim_K\operatorname{im}f_K\ge\dim_k\operatorname{im}f_k.$$
Consequently, for any bounded complex $P_*$ of finitely generated projective right-$A$ modules,
$$\sum_i(-1)^i\dim_K H_i(P_K)=\sum_i(-1)^i\dim_k H_i(P_k).$$
If additionally the complex is nonnegative, $\dim_k H_0(P_k)=1$ and $H_0(P_K)=0$, then
$$\dim_K H_1(P_K)\le\dim_k H_1(P_k)-1.$$
No choice principle or free basis for a projective module is assumed.
lem-ptfa-subgroup-scalar-extension-prese:
## Statement

Let $k$ be a commutative field, let $G$ be PTFA and let $H\le G$. Put $A=k[H]$, $B=k[G]$ and let $F\subseteq K$ be their Ore fraction division rings, with the compatible standard involutions fixing $k$. Let $M$ be a closed oriented three-manifold, with a supplied homomorphism $\pi_1(M_j)\to H$ on each component. Use the canonical based coefficient systems, with base vector $1$ and the standard transported Hermitian structure. Suppose $H_1(M;F)=0$.

Then $H_1(M;K)=0$, and there is the natural isomorphism
$$H_1(M;B)\cong H_1(M;A)\otimes_A B.$$
The maps $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ are injective. The coefficient Bockstein, oriented duality and evaluation define linking pairings $B_A$ with target $F/A$ and $B_B$ with target $K/B$, and their values satisfy
$$B_B(x\otimes1,y\otimes1)=j(B_A(x,y)),\qquad j:F/A\hookrightarrow K/B.$$
In particular a nonzero self-pairing remains nonzero after subgroup extension. Neither pairing is asserted nonsingular without its additional coefficient hypotheses. No choice principle is assumed.
lem-standard-infection-cobordisms-have-b:
## Statement

Let $P\cup\eta$ be a smooth oriented two-component link in $S^3$ with unknotted axis $\eta$, and let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot. Supply disjoint closed product tubes and positive meridian/preferred zero-linking-longitude peripheral data for the knots and axis. Write $P(K)$ for infection along $\eta$ with the untwisted companion $K$. For a knot $L$, write $M(L)$ for its actual chosen zero-longitude filling, with the orientation extending its exterior. Let $w=\operatorname{lk}(P,\eta)$.

There is a compact oriented smooth cobordism $E$ with
$$\partial E=M(P)\sqcup M(K)\sqcup(-M(P(K))).$$
For any commutative unital coefficient ring $R$, it has $H_1(E;R)=R$ and $H_2(E;R)=R^2$. The two first boundary components induce the displayed basis in degree two. If $s_L=\alpha_L\cap[M(L)]$ where $\alpha_L\in H^1(M(L);R)$ evaluates as $1$ on the positive meridian, then, in those coordinates,
$$i_*s_{P(K)}=i_*s_P+w\,i_*s_K.$$
In degree one the meridians of $P$, $K$ and $P(K)$ map to $1,w,1$, respectively.

Likewise, for any finite nonempty list of knots $K_1,\ldots,K_q$ with the same supplied peripheral data, there is a compact oriented smooth cobordism $C$ from $\bigsqcup_j M(K_j)$ to $M(K_1\#\cdots\#K_q)$, with $H_1(C;R)=R$ and $H_2(C;R)=R^q$. The incoming degree-two classes are its coordinate basis and the outgoing class maps to their sum. In particular, for $X=E$ or $C$, the outgoing inclusions are injective on $H_1,H_2$ and the union of incoming components surjects onto $H_2(X;R)$.

The peripheral and framing data are supplied, rather than selected by an existence theorem. Their subsequent construction and the homology assertions use no additional choice principle. This is an ordinary-coefficient assertion; arbitrary twisted-coefficient boundary generation is not asserted.
lem-zero-localized-intersection-rank-for:
## Statement

Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold with a supplied boundary collar. Supply a unital involution-stable inclusion $R\subseteq K$ into an involutive division ring and a based rank-one right-$R$ coefficient system on $W$, with unitary monodromy and the transported standard Hermitian form. Suppose
$$H_2(W;K)=\operatorname{im}\{H_2(\partial W;K)\longrightarrow H_2(W;K)\}.$$
Let $N$ be a finite union of connected boundary components, each satisfying $H_1(N_j;K)=0$, with its induced boundary orientation and coefficient system. On each component define the linking form by inverse coefficient Bockstein, inverse oriented cap duality and evaluation; let $B_N$ be their orthogonal sum. Then
$$B_N(x,y)=0\quad\text{whenever }x,y\in\ker\{H_1(N;R)\longrightarrow H_1(W;R)\}.$$
No choice axiom or finite CW structure is assumed. No vanishing condition is imposed on the unselected boundary components.
thm-integral-classical-blanchfield-self-:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a closed connected oriented Hausdorff topological three-manifold, with a specified based loop $\mu$ freely generating $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$. Use the associated right infinite-cyclic coefficient system, with first-loop-first convention and transport around $a$ given by left multiplication by $t^{-\phi(a)}$, where $\phi(\mu)=1$. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$, $\Lambda_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q[t,t^{-1}]$, and $\Lambda_p=\mathbb F_p[t,t^{-1}]$. All systems have their based standard parallel Hermitian structure with involution $t^*=t^{-1}$. Define $B_{\mathbb Z}$, $B_{\mathbb Q}$ and $B_p$ on the respective first local homology modules by inverse coefficient Bockstein, inverse oriented cap duality and evaluation, with targets $\mathbb Q(t)/\Lambda$, $\mathbb Q(t)/\Lambda_{\mathbb Q}$ and $\mathbb F_p(t)/\Lambda_p$.

These forms are defined on the whole respective first homology modules. There is a primitive annihilator $\Delta\in\mathbb Z[t]$, $\Delta(1)=1$, for $H_1(M;\Lambda)$. Put $\delta=\Delta^*$. For the actual coefficient images $x_{\mathbb Q},x_p,y_{\mathbb Q},y_p$ of any $x,y\in H_1(M;\Lambda)$,
$$B_{\mathbb Q}(x_{\mathbb Q},y_{\mathbb Q})=j\bigl(B_{\mathbb Z}(x,y)\bigr),\qquad B_p(x_p,y_p)=\rho_{p,\delta}\bigl(B_{\mathbb Z}(x,y)\bigr).$$
Here $j$ is the natural integral-to-rational quotient map, and $\rho_{p,\delta}$ is the well-defined fraction reduction on the $\delta$-annihilated subgroup, $[a/\delta]\mapsto[a_p/\delta_p]$. Its denominator is nonzero modulo every prime. Consequently, if $B_{\mathbb Z}(x,x)\ne0$, then $B_{\mathbb Q}(x_{\mathbb Q},x_{\mathbb Q})\ne0$ and $B_p(x_p,x_p)\ne0$ for all primes outside a finite explicit set. No choice principle, finite CW model, smoothness, Seifert presentation, or global rational-function reduction map is assumed.
thm-unimodular-intersection-pairs-force-:
## Statement

Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold with a supplied boundary collar, and put $M=\partial W$. Let $R\subseteq K$ be a unital involution-stable subring of an involutive division ring. Supply a based rank-one right-$R$ coefficient system $\mathcal R$ on $W$, with its base fiber identified with $R$, unitary monodromy and the transported standard Hermitian form. Write $H_*(W;R)$ and $H_*(W;K)$ for its homology and scalar-extended homology.

Define the equivariant intersection pairing $\lambda_R$ by sending $\bar p\in\overline{H_2(W;R)}$ through inverse relative cap duality to $H^2(W,M;\mathcal R^\vee)$, then into $H^2(W;\mathcal R^\vee)$, then evaluating on $q\in H_2(W;R)$. Here $\mathcal R^\vee$ is the intrinsic dual coefficient system, identified with the conjugate system by the supplied Hermitian form. Thus $\lambda_R(p,q)$ is conjugate-linear in $p$ and right-linear in $q$. Define $\lambda_K$ by the same construction over $K$.

Suppose $m\ge0$ and classes $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m,d_1,\ldots,d_m\in H_2(W;R)$ satisfy
$$\lambda_R(\ell_i,\ell_j)=0,\qquad\lambda_R(\ell_i,d_j)=\lambda_R(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij},$$
and suppose
$$\dim_K\bigl(H_2(W;K)/\operatorname{im}H_2(M;K)\bigr)\le2m.$$
Let $M_0$ be one connected boundary component with $H_1(M_0;K)=0$. Its coefficient Bockstein, oriented cap duality and evaluation define the linking form $B_0$ with values in $K/R$. Then
$$B_0(x,y)=0\quad\text{for all }x,y\in\ker\{H_1(M_0;R)\longrightarrow H_1(W;R)\}.$$
No vanishing condition on the other boundary components is imposed. No choice axiom, finite CW structure, or general noncommutative universal-coefficient theorem is assumed.
lem-concordance-annulus-induces-zero-sur:
## Statement

Let A be a proper annulus in a compact oriented 4-manifold W, with boundary knots K₀ and K₁ in the two boundary 3-spheres. Assume A has an oriented normal disk neighborhood A×D² whose endpoint framings are the preferred zero-linking longitudes. Let R be Z or R_n=Z[1/|n|], and assume each end S³→W is an R-homology isomorphism. Removing A×D² and attaching D²×S¹×I along the annular side, with ∂D² matched to the annulus longitude and the core matched to the normal meridian, produces a cobordism V from M(K₀) to M(K₁). The statement predicts that the boundary inclusions M(K_i)→V are R-homology isomorphisms. If W is simply connected, it also predicts that π₁(V) is normally generated by either endpoint knot-group image.
def-satellite-induced-concordance-operat:
## Definition

Let V=S¹×D² be the standard oriented solid torus, with oriented core, meridional disk and product longitude. A pattern is a smooth oriented knot P in the interior of V. Its winding number w(P) is its algebraic intersection with an oriented meridional disk, equivalently the coefficient of the core in [P]∈H₁(V;Z). For a smooth oriented knot K in S³, let e_K:V→S³ be a zero-framed tubular embedding carrying the core to K and carrying the meridian and product longitude to the positive meridian and preferred longitude of K. The satellite knot P(K) is e_K(P).

When concordance preservation has been established, the formula [K]↦[P(K)] defines a set map on each of C_sm, C_top, C_ex and C^{1/n}. The solid-torus meridian is strong winding number ±1 for P if, after V is embedded as the standard unknotted solid torus and P(U) denotes the resulting closure, that meridian normally generates π₁(S³\P(U)). Normal generation means that the smallest normal subgroup containing the element is the whole group. Strong winding number ±1 is a separate condition from ordinary winding number ±1. No additivity or homomorphism property is part of this definition.
lem-ptfa-localization-kills-first-homolo:
## Statement

Let $N$ be a compact connected Hausdorff topological manifold, with boundary allowed, and let $k$ be a commutative field with $\dim_k H_1(N;k)=1$. Let $\phi:\pi_1(N)\to G$ be nontrivial with $G$ PTFA, and let $K$ be the Ore fraction division ring of $k[G]$. Then $H_0(N;K)=H_1(N;K)=0$. No choice principle or finite CW model for $N$ is assumed.
lem-standard-infection-cobordism-adjunct:
## Statement

Let $E$ be the actual standard infection cobordism from $M(P)\sqcup M(K)$ to $M(P(K))$, constructed from the two surgery products by identifying $N(\eta)$ with the filling solid torus $V_K$. Supply the oriented product tubes and peripheral paths, with $\mu_\eta=\lambda_K$ and $\lambda_\eta=\mu_K$ on the common torus, where $\lambda_K$ is the companion's preferred longitude. No winding-number condition is needed. The inclusion-induced homomorphism is onto and induces
$$\pi_1(M(P(K)))/\langle\!\langle\lambda_K\rangle\!\rangle\ \cong\ \pi_1(E).$$
The marked companion meridian and pattern-axis core have the same image in $\pi_1(E)$, with the supplied base paths.

More generally, if a connected manifold $W$ with supplied boundary collar is glued to $E$ along the marked outgoing component $M(P(K))$, the inclusion-induced map is onto and gives
$$\pi_1(W)/\langle\!\langle i_*(\lambda_K)\rangle\!\rangle\ \cong\ \pi_1(W\cup_{M(P(K))}E).$$
Changing a peripheral base path changes the relator by conjugation and leaves its normal closure unchanged. The statements hold for topological collared $W$ as well as smooth $W$ and use no choice axiom.
thm-cdr-concordance-categories-form-abel:
## Statement

Assume AC_ω. Under connected sum, each of C_sm, C_top, C_ex and C^{1/n} is an abelian group. The identity is the class of the unknot, and the inverse of [K] is the class of the reverse mirror of K. Each category retains the ambient and coefficient conditions in its definition.
thm-ptfa-localized-boundary-intersection:
## Statement

Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented Hausdorff topological four-manifold and put $M=\partial W$, allowing $M$ empty. Let $k$ be a commutative field, $G$ a PTFA group, and $\phi:\pi_1(W)\to G$ a supplied coefficient homomorphism. Write $K$ for the fraction division ring of $k[G]$, with its standard involution, and use the induced rank-one right-coefficient systems. Suppose $\dim_kH_1(M_j;k)=1$ for each connected component $M_j$ of $M$. Then
$$\dim_K\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(M;K)\to H_2(W;K)\}\le\dim_k\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(M;k)\to H_2(W;k)\}.$$
All dimensions in the formula are finite. No choice axiom, smoothness, triangulation, or supplied finite CW model of $W$ is assumed.
lem-finite-winding-zero-infection-towers:
## Statement

Fix $n\ge1$ and a finite marked smooth infection sequence $J_{j+1}=P_j(J_j)$, $0\le j<n$, with unknotted axes $\eta_j$ and winding number zero. Supply compatible product tubes, peripheral paths and finite disk-band Seifert-surface models with local ambient roundings for all knots $J_j$ and $P_j(U)$. Let $E_j$ be their actual standard infection cobordisms. Let $W_n$ be any compact connected oriented topological four-manifold with a supplied collared boundary component $M(J_n)$, and form
$$W_j=W_{j+1}\cup_{M(J_{j+1})}E_j\qquad(j=n-1,\ldots,0)$$
using the marked collars. Other boundary components of $W_n$ are allowed. Base paths are supplied coherently through the finite gluings. Write $\mu_j$ for the positive meridian of $J_j$ and $G_j=\pi_1(W_j)$.

For $0\le k<n$, inclusion induces an epimorphism $q_k:G_{k+1}\to G_k$ and a natural isomorphism
$$G_{k+1}/G_{k+1}^{(n-k+1)}\cong G_k/G_k^{(n-k+1)}.$$
Moreover $\mu_k\in G_k^{(n-k)}$. For any supplied finite commutative-ring list $R_0,\ldots,R_n$, define the mixed series by
$$P^0G=G,\qquad P^{i+1}G=\ker\!\left(P^iG\longrightarrow(P^iG/[P^iG,P^iG])\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R_i\right).$$
The same $q_k$ identifies $G_{k+1}/P^iG_{k+1}$ with $G_k/P^iG_k$ for $i\le n-k+1$, and identifies $P^iG_{k+1}/P^{i+1}G_{k+1}$ with $P^iG_k/P^{i+1}G_k$ for $0\le i<n-k+1$. These are assertions for the actual inclusion maps. No nontriviality or order assertion about a meridian in a mixed quotient is included; such an assertion requires the separate Blanchfield argument. No choice principle or smoothing of $W_n$ is assumed.
lem-satellite-connected-sum-substitution:
## Statement

Let P be a pattern and let K be a knot. Choose a transverse meridional disk for P and a short product slab about it. Form a pattern P_K by replacing all strands of P across that slab by parallel untwisted copies of a long-knot representative of K, with the individual strand orientations inherited from P; this is simultaneous companion insertion, rather than tying K into just one arc. For every knot J, the satellite P(K#J) is isotopic as an oriented knot to P_K(J). The pattern P_K has the same winding number as P.
lem-satellite-operator-preserves-concord:
## Statement

Let P⊂S¹×D² be a smooth oriented pattern. If oriented knots K₀ and K₁ are concordant in one of the four categories C_sm, C_top, C_ex or C^{1/n}, then P(K₀) and P(K₁) are concordant in the same category. Thus P induces a well-defined set map on each of these concordance sets.
lem-strong-winding-stable-under-companio:
## Statement

Let P be a pattern of strong winding number ±1. For every oriented knot K, regard P(K) as the pattern obtained by tying K into each strand of P in the companion solid torus. Then this new pattern P(K) also has strong winding number ±1. A pattern obtained from any strong-winding pattern by taking connected sum with a local knot also has strong winding number ±1.
thm-integral-pair-data-yield-blanchfield:
## Statement

Let $V$ be a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold with boundary a chosen zero-longitude surgery $M(J)$. Suppose
$$H_1(V;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z,\qquad H_2(V;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{2r}.$$
Put $\pi=\pi_1(V)$ and $\Pi_s=\pi/\pi^{(s)}$, where $s\ge0$ and the superscript denotes the ordinary derived series. Supply classes $x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_r\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\Pi_s])$ satisfying
$$\lambda(x_i,x_j)=0,\qquad\lambda(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}.$$
These are actual integral intersection-pair data; existence of such data is not asserted.

Form $W$ by finitely many oriented attachments of standard connected-sum or infection cobordisms, allowing their orientation reversals, along each piece's marked outgoing surgery component. Use the supplied peripheral models in those constructions. Let $\phi:\pi_1(W)\to G$ be a supplied homomorphism to a PTFA group whose restriction to $\pi_1(V)$ factors through $\Pi_s$. In particular the factorization is automatic if $G^{(s)}=1$. Let $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ for a prime $p$, put $A=k[G]$, and let $K$ be its fraction division ring with standard involution.

Then there are image classes $\ell_i,d_i\in H_2(W;A)$ with
$$\lambda_A(\ell_i,\ell_j)=0,\qquad\lambda_A(\ell_i,d_j)=\lambda_A(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij},$$
and both cokernel dimensions satisfy
$$\dim_K\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(\partial W;K)\to H_2(W;K)\}\le\dim_k\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(\partial W;k)\to H_2(W;k)\}\le2r.$$
For every boundary component $M_0$ with nontrivial restricted homomorphism, $H_1(M_0;K)=0$ and its Bockstein-duality pairing has
$$B_0(a,b)=0\quad\text{for all }a,b\in\ker\{H_1(M_0;A)\to H_1(W;A)\}.$$
Consequently every boundary class with nonzero self-pairing has nonzero image in $H_1(W;A)$. The theorem applies to locally flat topological bordisms as well as smooth ones and introduces no choice principle.
thm-winding-zero-infection-preserves-cla:
## Statement

Let $P\cup\eta\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented two-component link with unknotted axis and $\operatorname{lk}(P,\eta)=0$. Supply the disjoint closed product tubes, positive meridians and preferred zero-linking longitudes. For a smooth oriented companion knot $K$, form the untwisted infection $P(K)$ and the standard infection cobordism $E$ with oriented boundary $M(P)\sqcup M(K)\sqcup(-M(P(K)))$, where $M$ denotes the actual preferred zero-longitude surgery.

Let $k$ be any commutative field, $\Lambda=k[t,t^{-1}]$ with involution $\bar t=t^{-1}$, and $F=k(t)$. Use the coefficient system on $E$ sending the positive meridian of $P$ to $t$, and its restrictions to the boundary, with the standard based Hermitian form. On $M(P)$ and $M(P(K))$ these are their positive classical infinite-cyclic systems. The two inclusions give isomorphisms
$$H_1(M(P);\Lambda)\xrightarrow{i_P}H_1(E;\Lambda)\xleftarrow{i_{P(K)}}H_1(M(P(K));\Lambda).$$
Consequently $T=i_{P(K)}^{-1}i_P$ is an isometry of their classical Blanchfield pairings:
$$B_{P(K)}(Tx,Ty)=B_P(x,y).$$
With base paths through the common pattern exterior fixed as part of the peripheral data, $T[\eta]=[\mu_K]$, where the companion meridian on the infected side is oriented by the prescribed longitude-to-meridian identification. Thus a nonzero axis self-pairing remains nonzero on this companion-meridian class. For another base path the corresponding equality is conjugated by the induced power of $t$, which preserves its self-pairing. No choice axiom or finite CW model for the surgery manifolds is assumed.
lem-cdr-zero-surgery-pattern-homology-co:
## Statement

Let P be an oriented pattern of winding n≠0 and K an oriented knot. If P(U) bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold B whose oriented boundary is identified with the standard oriented S³ and H_i(B;R_n)≅H_i(B⁴;R_n) for every i, then for every K the zero surgeries M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly R_n-homology cobordant. For the positive meridians determined by the supplied orientations, their images in the cobordism satisfy [mu_K]=n[mu_{P(K)}]; in particular they differ by a unit of R_n. This is a winding-unit meridian comparison, not a claim of literal equality for arbitrary winding. If P has strong winding number ±1 and P(U) is pseudo-slice (respectively locally flat topologically slice), then M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly (respectively topologically) homology cobordant through a 4-manifold whose fundamental group is normally generated by the image of the fundamental group of either boundary component. The category and closure hypotheses are separate and cannot be inferred from winding alone.
thm-amenable-von-neumann-l2-flatness:
## Statement

Let G be a countable discrete amenable group. For every right CG-module M and every integer q>0, the N G-von Neumann dimension of Tor_q^{CG}(M,N G) is zero. This dimension-flatness statement does not say that the Tor module itself is zero.
thm-l2-signature-theorem-for-closed-four:
## Statement

Let X be a closed oriented smooth 4-manifold, Γ a discrete group, and φ:π₁(X)→Γ a homomorphism. Then the von Neumann signature of the NΓ-coefficient intersection form equals the ordinary signature:
sign_Γ^(2)(X,φ)=sign(X).
lem-amenable-D-R-l2-dimension-estimate:
## Statement

Let R be Q or F_p, let Γ be a countable discrete amenable group in Strebel's class D(R), and let C_* be a bounded-below chain complex of right ZΓ-modules whose C_i are finitely generated free for i≤n. Give R the trivial Γ-action. If H_i(C_*⊗_{ZΓ}R)=0 for every i≤n, then H_i(C_*⊗_{ZΓ}NΓ) has von Neumann dimension zero for every i≤n. This is a dimension-zero conclusion and does not assert that the L²-homology module vanishes.
lem-cdr-weak-injectivity-and-auxiliary-p:
## Statement

Let P be a pattern of nonzero winding n. If P(U) is smoothly slice in an R_n-homology 4-ball, then P is weakly injective on C^{1/n}, meaning P(K)=P(U) implies K=U in that category. If P has strong winding number ±1 and P(U) is pseudo-slice (respectively locally flat topologically slice), then P is weakly injective on C_ex (respectively C_top). In ordinary smooth concordance, if P(U) is smoothly slice in standard B⁴ and P has strong winding number ±1, then P is weakly injective on C_sm provided the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture holds.

For any pattern P and knots K,J with P(K)=P(J) in one of these concordance groups, the connected-sum reduction constructs a pattern R for which R(−K#J) is concordant to U, whose closure R(U)=−P(K)#P(K) is ribbon, and whose winding w(R)=w(P). If P is strong winding ±1, then R is strong winding ±1. This reduction turns injectivity of P into weak injectivity of R; it does not assert that P itself is weakly injective without the closure hypotheses above.
lem-higher-order-blanchfield-pairings-ar:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a closed oriented three-manifold, with a specified coefficient homomorphism $\phi:\pi_1(M_j)\to\Gamma$ on each component $M_j$, where $\Gamma$ is PTFA. Let $k=\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field, put $A=k[\Gamma]$, and let $K$ be its fraction division ring with the involution fixing $k$ and inverting group elements. Let $A\subseteq R\subseteq K$ be an involution-stable unital intermediate ring, and assume $H_1(M;K)=0$.

Then $H_1(M;R)$ is an $R$-torsion module and the coefficient Bockstein, oriented duality and evaluation define its Blanchfield pairing with target $K/R$. This pairing is nonsingular provided that on each component at least one of the following holds: every right ideal of $R$ is principal; $H_0(M_j;R)=0$; or the image of $\phi|_{\pi_1(M_j)}$ is cyclic. The last condition includes the usual integral infinite-cyclic coefficient case $R=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, without asserting that this ring is a principal ideal domain. No choice principle is assumed.
lem-l2-rho-invariant-bordism-independenc:
## Statement

Let M be a closed oriented 3-manifold, Γ a discrete group, and φ:π₁(M)→Γ. If (W₀,ψ₀) and (W₁,ψ₁) are compact oriented 4-manifolds with boundary M over which φ extends, then sign_Γ^(2)(W₀,ψ₀)−sign(W₀)=sign_Γ^(2)(W₁,ψ₁)−sign(W₁). Hence the signature defect depends only on (M,φ).
thm-cheeger-gromov-uniform-rho-bound:
## Statement

For every closed oriented 3-manifold M there exists a finite constant C_M such that for every discrete group Γ and every homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→Γ for which the rho invariant is defined, |ρ(M,φ)|≤C_M. The constant may depend on M but not on Γ or φ.
lem-cha-kim-integral-solvability-and-bla:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$. Supply a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold $V$ with boundary a marked knot zero surgery, $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ and $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$, and exactly $r$ integral pairs $x_i,y_i\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi/\pi^{(n)}])$, $\pi=\pi_1(V)$, satisfying $\lambda(x_i,x_j)=0$ and $\lambda(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Form $W$ by any finite sequence of the actual marked standard connected-sum and winding-zero infection cobordism adjunctions along outgoing knot-surgery components, including orientation reversals, using supplied smooth peripheral products and collars. Let $\phi:\pi_1(W)\to\Gamma$ have PTFA target and restrict on $V$ through $\pi/\pi^{(n)}$. Take $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ and put $A=k[\Gamma]$, with involutive Ore fraction division ring $K$ and the based standard parallel Hermitian structure.

The image pairs $\ell_i,d_i\in H_2(W;A)$ satisfy $\lambda(\ell_i,\ell_j)=0$ and $\lambda(\ell_i,d_j)=\lambda(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij}$. Their localized boundary-intersection cokernel has dimension at most $2r$. For each boundary component $M_0$ on which $\phi$ is nontrivial, $H_1(M_0;K)=0$, its coefficient Bockstein–duality linking form is defined, and its actual inclusion kernel is isotropic:
$$B_{M_0}(z,w)=0\quad\text{for all }z,w\in\ker\{H_1(M_0;A)\to H_1(W;A)\}.$$
Thus every boundary class with nonzero self-pairing survives in $H_1(W;A)$ and lies outside every isotropic submodule. If a component's coefficient image is cyclic, its form additionally has the nonsingularity furnished by the cyclic-image coefficient theorem; no unrestricted PTFA nonsingularity is asserted.

For a finite forest of iterated winding-zero infections with these initial data, suppose each top meridian generates $H_1(W_n;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ up to sign, and each pattern-axis integral classical self-pairing is nonzero. Use the actual intermediate $W_j$, rational mixed coefficients through index $n$, and one bottom field $\mathbb F_p$. For every odd prime outside the explicit finite exceptional set of the axis values, every branch meridian has a nonzero class in $P^{n-j}\pi_1(W_j)/P^{n-j+1}\pi_1(W_j)$, of infinite order when $j>0$ and order $p$ when $j=0$. All these conclusions hold for the supplied locally flat topological bordisms and smooth bordisms without a choice principle. Existence of the initial $V$ and its lifted pairs from a concordance relation is a separate hypothesis, as are analytic rho invariance and signature vanishing.
thm-amenable-signature-vanishing-for-sol:
## Statement

Let K be a knot and W an integral (n+1/2)-solution for M(K). Let R be Q or F_p, let G be an amenable group in Strebel's class D(R) with G^(n+1)={e}, and let φ:π₁(M(K))→G extend over W. Assume φ sends a meridian of K to an infinite-order element of G. Then the rho invariant ρ(M(K),φ) vanishes.
thm-cochran-davis-ray-strong-winding-inj:
## Statement

Let P be a pattern of nonzero winding number n. Then P induces an injective function C^{1/n}→C^{1/n}. If P has strong winding number ±1, then it induces injective functions C_ex→C_ex and C_top→C_top. If, in addition, the smooth 4-sphere has a unique smooth structure up to diffeomorphism, then P induces an injective function C_sm→C_sm. No sliceness hypothesis on P(U) is required in this theorem; the proof constructs an auxiliary pattern with ribbon closure.
lem-cha-kim-higher-order-rho-bound-and-c:
## Statement

Assume full AC and the winding-zero and nonzero axis Blanchfield self-pairing hypotheses of Cha–Kim. For each finite stage of their iterated-infection construction, the companion knots can be chosen so that the relevant higher-order rho contribution has a fixed sign and dominates the sum of all remaining terms, using a uniform Cheeger–Gromov bound and signature functions supported on selected unit-circle arcs between realized reciprocal-polynomial roots. Relatively prime Alexander hypotheses belong to the separate Theorem C comparison of distinct patterns; they are not hypotheses of Theorems A or B.
thm-cha-kim-winding-zero-iterates-infini:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let P⊂S¹×D² be a winding-zero pattern. Assume the axis has nonzero classical Blanchfield self-pairing in the Alexander module of P(U), with the convention that the axis defines the class paired with itself. For either the locally flat topological concordance group C_top or the smooth concordance group C_sm, let Pⁿ be the n-fold composition of the induced satellite set map, with P⁰ the identity. For every n≥0, the quotient ⟨Pⁿ(C)⟩/⟨Pⁿ⁺¹(C)⟩ has infinite rank, where ⟨S⟩ denotes the subgroup generated by S and rank means dim_Q(A⊗_Z Q) for an abelian group A. For n≥1, Pⁿ is not a group homomorphism under the same hypotheses. No pairwise-coprime Alexander-polynomial assumption is part of these Theorems A and B.
